title: PRD: Progressive Quality Slices and Gradual Degrade Playbook for Hosted Inference
creator: Ava Clarke
description: This PRD defines a unified approach to progressive degradation for Redwood hosted endpoints (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Goal: provide configurable quality bands that let platform operators and customers trade latency/cost vs. output quality with safe fallbacks and measurable acceptance criteria. The feature must be backward-compatible, expose a simple opt-in API parameter, and include an operational playbook for canarying and rollback.
scope: In scope: API surface for quality_bands parameter (server-side default + per-request override), routing policies to select model variants or quantized versions, telemetry and eval gating for quality regressions, canary & ramp plan, SDK & docs updates, billing labels for banded pricing. Endpoints covered: chat (conversation), completions, embeddings, rerank. Also includes console UI for per-tenant default band and visualization of banded cost/quality tradeoffs.
out_of_scope: Per-customer private deployment changes (Private control plane UI), advanced auto-ML selection of band thresholds, on-prem hardware scheduling changes beyond runtime knobs, persistent user-specific evaluation storage (will be part of future Optimize work).
requirements: API: add optional request field 'quality_profile' with enum values ["high", "balanced", "cost_saver"] and a server-side tenant default override.
Routing: server selects a model variant/quantization level based on profile and current capacity when profile is not 'high'.
Telemetry: emit tags 'quality_profile' and 'served_variant' on traces and token metrics; add per-profile cost and p50/p95/p99 latency aggregates in the Console.
Eval gating: integrate evaluation harness to run nightly quality checks on representative prompt sets per endpoint and alert on >2% top-line regression vs baseline for 'balanced' and 'high' bands.
Fallbacks: if chosen variant fails or exceeds latency budget, automatically fall back to the next higher-quality variant until success or hard fail with descriptive error code.
SDKs & Docs: JS and Python SDK must accept quality_profile and surface clear migration guidance; docs must include examples and recommended defaults.
Billing: emitted metering tags to map request to band for downstream cost attribution and per-token billing adjustments.
Console: tenant-level default settings UI and a banded cost/latency visualization chart for last 7/30 days.
Canary: support gradual ramping knob (percentage of traffic) by tenant/route for the new profiles.
Operational runbooks: start/stop canary steps, regression thresholds, and rollback actions.
Security: ensure quality_profile cannot be injected to escalate tenant privileges; validate parameter at gateway.
Compatibility: default behavior when quality_profile omitted must match current cost/quality behavior (no regression).
acceptance_criteria: API contract: documented swagger/contract for quality_profile and server-side override; backward-compatible when omitted.
Routing correctness: for a test matrix of 30 synthetic requests across endpoints, recorded served_variant matches expected mapping for each profile 99/100 times.
Latency SLOs: p99 latency for 'balanced' band within 1.3x baseline p99; 'high' band within 1.05x baseline p99 under normal load.
Cost: measured per-token cost for 'cost_saver' band is at least 25% lower than 'high' for matched traffic in controlled tests.
Quality regressions: nightly eval shows <1.5% regression for 'balanced' and <0.5% for 'high' across representative eval sets; any failing eval triggers rollback criteria.
Fallback behavior: simulated failure of lower-quality variant results in automatic fallback with meaningful logs and error codes; no customer-visible 5xx increase during controlled chaos test.
Telemetry: Console surfaces per-profile latency/cost curves and traces include quality_profile and served_variant tags for all requests in the canary window.
SDKs: JS/Python SDKs pass integration tests and examples in docs are validated by QA.
Billing: metering tags verified end-to-end to billing pipeline for sample traffic; accounting reports match expected band assignments.
Security: gateway rejects invalid values for quality_profile and no escalation paths are possible in penetration tests.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary (10% traffic) for engineering tenants + synthetic traffic for 72h. Phase 2: Tenant opt-in beta (select 5 customers, 1-2 routes each) for 2 weeks with daily eval checks. Phase 3: Gradual platform-wide enablement as tenant defaults (25%, 50%, 100%) across 2-week ramps, gated by metrics and manual signoffs. Final GA: open to all tenants with docs and SDK release. At every phase we run nightly eval jobs, observe p99 latencies and cost delta, and confirm no quality regression beyond thresholds. Use feature flag 'quality-bands-v1' for fast rollback.

notes: Design tradeoff: exposing explicit profiles is easier to understand for customers than opaque autoscaling decisions; may revisit with Optimize later.
We deliberately avoid per-tenant ML-driven band tuning in v1 to reduce blast radius and simplify rollbacks.
If nightly evals show slow drift, plan includes immediate freeze of tenant defaults and targeted rollbacks for affected routes.
